result.summary:
I traced who uses the rung floor's certified numbers and the H5 drivers' certified outputs, in the archive and on origin/main. I ran no engine. I read archive members to stdout or in memory and wrote only my own notes (under <SCRATCH>/covtrace/lens_notes/downstream-reach/).

(a) Rung floor, archive. Every load-bearing consumer takes only the lower end of the interval, Z_lo = 7.7592917375327855e-3, as a divisor of upper bounds:
- D3: d3_amend_v2, d3_perc_decay and d3_rn_unif all read it from H3_RUNG_FLOOR.md. It gives κ_far ≤ 0.68, B_remote ≤ 21.9279·r³ and B2-far ≤ 17.6802·r³.
- D1 v2.2 then consumes those D3 numbers.
- D1's C_RN is computed against c_Z·r², not against Z_lo. The rung floor's only role there is the check that Z_lo > c_Z·r².

The upper end 1.1468646473404396e-2 is never load-bearing. It appears only in drift checks, the QMC consistency check, LPW v3/v4 consistency checks and LPW v3's labeled ESTIMATE.

The mut_rung_floor_* transcripts belong to an LPW/H1 mutation family on the λ eigenfloor. They are not about h3_rung_floor.

(a) H5, archive. The drivers never read the rung floor. Z_lo = max(c_Z·r², Z_own.a), and Z_own.a = 0 in every banked transcript, so Z_lo = c_Z·r².
- The certified output that moves downstream is I_hi in h5_totals*.json. D1's gates and h5_promote use it as an upper bound; I_lo appears only in containment checks.
- The twin-derived Z_own.b = 1.3970321600e-2 is hard-coded as an upper bound on Z in H5 helper drivers and in two Stage-E scripts that certify lower bounds on ρ_w. No file I found cites those two scripts' results.

(b) origin/main.
- Neither H3_RUNG_FLOOR.md, h3_rung_floor.py nor any mut_rung_floor file exists in the tree; they appear only as manifest or receipt rows.
- The citations sit in incoming/ copies (D1 v2.2 receipts and gate, the D3 amendment v2 and PERC-DECAY, RETURN_06, the D1 v2.3 draft and d1_falsify_v4, CL-OBL-001, CL-PIN-001, H5_ZBAND), in docs/QUEUE_RECONCILIATION_20260927.md and in docs/public-math catalogs.
- H5_ZBAND consumes the band floor and band ceiling, not the rung floor.
- sources-14 links to commit 7caac254, which is not an ancestor of origin/main. That commit holds d3_rn_unif.py and cov_exact.py as plain files, byte-identical to the archive copies, so the draft's 'only inside a chunked archive' does not hold for those two files.

I did not judge any theorem.

result.summary: I tried to refute the draft's classification headline and could not; it stands. (i) No class-3 iv value feeds CK4–CK6, CERT_LO or CERT_HI in h3_c0_certificate.py. (ii) Both h3_rung_floor's library iv Grams and h5's twin carry class-3 values (or their analogue) used two-sided, so neither certified path is class-1/2-only. (iii) The Lattice twin matches cov_exact's iv shape and tail formula at orders ≤ 8. However, the draft calls lambda_q the 'class-2 analogue', and that is wrong for odd q: it sums signed w·k^q, which returns about 1e-98, and the Taylor-model remainder calls it with odd q in both StationBox and CoarseBox. This is a new gap, separate from the library defect, and its effect on any printed number was not assessed. (iv) The draft misses no iv evaluator call. But it omits the one_minus_a2_poisson(mode='iv') gates in all four H3 engines. It also describes several files as having no library call (or as not naming it) when they reach it indirectly in mpf mode. Minor precision fixes: a6 enters only det G0; twin orders used are 9–12, not 9–18; the twin also evaluates at 0; c2's sentinel has both arguments nonzero; only the h5_run*.py drivers run at dps 40. Sources are under <SCRATCH>/covtrace/src/K3_SIDE24_LB/. My own check scripts are <SCRATCH>/covtrace/lens_notes/adversarial/lambda_q_check.py and rung_enum.py. lambda_q_check.py re-implements the formulas without importing any engine and ran under the scratchpad venv's mpmath 1.3.0; rung_enum.py is pure Python. The engines' own mpmath version is UNKNOWN. No engine was run.

findings.claim: lambda_q is not an upper bound for odd q: it sums signed w*k^q, which cancels to about 1e-98, and the Taylor-model remainder calls it with odd q, so the draft's description of it as the 'class-2 analogue' fails for odd q.
findings.evidence: h5_kernel.py:79 uses kj**q, not abs(kj)**q (contrast h3_band_ceil.py:331 abs(kk)**n). :538 sets R = lambda_q(n+TD+1)*eta^(TD+1)/(TD+1)!. TD = 5 in StationBox (:559) and 6 in CoarseBox (:1328); cross_tm (:546-549) passes per-axis orders. Example: CoarseBox row 'f' (xjet(0), :722-723) against pin 'f' gives tm_factor(0) and so lambda_q(7). R.b enters the bounds at :243, :269, :312 and in coarse_fine_hi at :1631, :1634, :1643, :1649. My own re-implementation (lambda_q_check.py) gives lambda_q.b = 1.21e-98 at q=7 vs (1/Z)sum w|k|^7 = 38.30; 1.19e-97 at q=9 vs 306.4; 1.37e-96 at q=11 vs 3063.9. Even q agree exactly (15, 105, 945, 10395).
findings.proposed_wording: lambda_q (L75-82) is a class-2-style majorant only for even q. It sums w*k^q with the sign of k (L79), so for odd q the +-k terms cancel and it returns about 1e-98, not an upper bound. L538 calls it with odd q = n + TD + 1 (odd n in StationBox, TD = 5; even n in CoarseBox, TD = 6), so those Taylor-model remainders are effectively zero. This gap is separate from the library defect; its effect on any printed number was not assessed.

findings.claim: The kernel evaluates twin orders only up to 11 or 12, not up to 18.
findings.evidence: h5_kernel.py:525 sets NMAX = 4+TD+2, and :528-529 evaluate orders 0..NMAX; TD is 5 or 6 (:559, :1328, :1615); the twin's ceiling is 18 (:86); lambda_q is called with q up to 4+TD+1 <= 11 (:538).
findings.proposed_wording: Orders 9-12 come only from the twin (NMAX = 4 + TD + 2 at L525, with TD = 5 or 6). The library stops at order 8, and the twin allows up to 18 (L86).

findings.claim: Not every twin argument is nonzero: PinFrame also caches t = 0, and KernelSeries also evaluates at 'zero' for the y-jet x y-jet entries; the class-3-analogue values are the +-r M-S entries and the dxM/dxS/dyv cross terms.

result.summary: Archive-wide completeness check of a2136bc0.zip (sha256 a2136bc0…2b5b, 1,794 members). I read everything in place: the zip and its nested zips in memory, plus the verified extracted .py tree. Nothing was executed and nothing was unpickled. The draft's counts and lists hold up.
